On s'y assoit pour dire comment ça va, v: You sit here to say how you really are. The village began where people started listening to one another.
On s'y assoit sous un arbre pour regarde: You sit here under a tree to watch your thoughts go by. The island's most restless people come out lighter.
Le flatteur, le bavard, le radin : trent: The flatterer, the chatterbox, the miser: thirty portraits hung under the arcades. Everyone recognises their neighbour.
Il ne commande ni au vent ni aux vagues,: He commands neither the wind nor the waves, only his lamp. Worried sailors climb up to see him before setting out.
On y soigne la peur et la tristesse comm: Fear and sadness are treated here the way a fever is, by talking. Nobody is ashamed to go in.
Un homme s'y est enfermé avec ses livres: A man shut himself away here with his books to study himself. His notebooks circulate, and everyone finds themselves in them.
Six tiroirs pour six passions simples, e: Six drawers for six simple passions, and all their mixtures. An anger is taken apart here like a clock.
On y parle aux malades au lieu de les at: Here the sick are talked to instead of tied up. Several have gone home, which was thought impossible.
Une grande carte où chaque région a sa t: A large map where each region has its task. Healers know why a blow here changes speech, and there character.
Joie, peur, dégoût : des portraits de ge: Joy, fear, disgust: portraits of people and animals side by side. Foreigners who land make themselves understood from the quay.
On y mesure le temps d'une pensée au cen: The time of a thought is measured here to the hundredth of a second. The soul has become an object of experiment.
On y revoit la leçon le lendemain, puis: The lesson is reviewed the next day, then three days later, then the following week. The island's schoolchildren no longer forget their times tables.
Le chenil à la clochette: The kennel with the little bell
Les chiens du berger accourent au premie: The shepherd's dogs come running at the first tinkle. You learn here how a habit takes hold, and how it comes undone.
Le cabinet au divan: The consulting room with the couch
On s'y allonge et on dit ce qui vient. T: You lie down and say whatever comes. Not everyone believes in the method, but everyone talks about it.
On y repère tôt les écoliers qui peinent: Struggling pupils are spotted early here, to help them, not to sort them. The rule is posted above the blackboard.
On y sait ce qu'un enfant peut comprendr: Here they know what a child can understand at each age, and that it first needs safe arms. Parents learn as much as the little ones.
Chacun y choisit son ouvrage et voit ses: Everyone chooses their own work and sees their progress on the wall. Nobody drags their feet to come.
On y vote derrière un rideau, sans voir: You vote behind a curtain, without seeing what the queue is doing. The island's majorities have changed their tune.
On y cherche le métier qui va à chaque t: Here they look for the trade that suits each temperament, without horoscopes. The shy one keeps the lighthouse, the chatterbox runs the market.
Sieste, cerfs-volants et parties de boul: Naps, kites and games of boules: the island has understood that you work better when you stop. The power station runs slow that day.
